name: hf-open-llm-v2-score-matrix
description: A cleaned 4486 x 7 score matrix derived from the public Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard v2 (April 2026 snapshot). Each row corresponds to one model evaluated on six benchmarks: IFEval, BBH, MATH (Level 5), GPQA, MUSR, and MMLU-Pro. All scores are normalized to [0,1]. Cleaning steps: rows with any missing benchmark score were dropped, models with upstream flagged=true were excluded, and duplicates were removed by model identifier. Population breakdown: 39 percent fine-tunes, 38 percent merges, 16 percent chat models, 7 percent pretrained base.
citeAs: Anonymous Authors. Minimal Sufficient Benchmarks: Score Imputation for Cost-Efficient LLM Leaderboards. NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track (under review).
rai:dataCollection: Programmatic download from the public Hugging Face Hub dataset open-llm-leaderboard/contents (parquet format) on April 2026. No human subjects, no PII, no scraping of restricted data. The data consists entirely of aggregate evaluation scores of publicly released models on publicly released benchmarks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Step 1: drop rows with any null benchmark score. Step 2: drop rows where upstream flagged=True. Step 3: deduplicate by model identifier (keep first). Step 4: convert reported percentages to [0,1] floats. Reproducible from the upstream source via documentation in the accompanying repository.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation. Scores are deterministic outputs of running benchmarks against models on the EleutherAI evaluation harness as published by the upstream leaderboard maintainers.
rai:dataUseCases: Studying redundancy structure across benchmark suites; per-subset rank-fidelity analysis for leaderboard maintainers; power analyses for benchmark-design decisions; construct validity research on LLM evaluation; meta-evaluation of evaluation methodology.
rai:dataLimitation: (1) Six-column scope, exhaustive subset search becomes intractable beyond d~12. (2) Population skew: ~39 percent fine-tunes and ~38 percent merges, both inheriting performance profiles from base models. (3) Snapshot in time: April 2026 only. (4) Scores capture statistical redundancy among benchmarks, not scientific redundancy of underlying constructs.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The score_matrix.csv snapshot is dated April 2026 and is not auto-refreshed. Quarterly refresh is recommended for users applying the imputation framework to current data. A practical heuristic: a benchmark whose novelty (1 - R^2_CV) drops below 0.1 on a current snapshot has saturated. The release is versioned in the repository.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables compute-efficient LLM evaluation, potentially saving substantial GPU-hours across the research community. By documenting redundancy structure honestly, it discourages the proliferation of near-duplicate benchmarks.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The dataset contains no personal or sensitive information; entries are aggregate scores of language models.
